title: The shipping container and waterfront megaprojects (1955)

steps.claim: Malcom McLean buys Pan-Atlantic Steamship

test.source: purchase completed 1955 (Levinson, The Box)

steps.claim: The Ideal X sails with 58 containers

test.source: Newark to Houston, 26 Apr 1956

steps.link_why: McLean converted the ship for his trailers-as-boxes plan

steps.claim: Loading costs fall from $5.83 to about $0.16 a ton

test.source: cost comparison for the Ideal X voyage (Levinson, The Box)

steps.link_why: the comparison is for this voyage

steps.claim: Sea-Land supplies the Vietnam War by container

test.source: Sea-Land contract for Cam Ranh Bay, 1966–67

steps.claim: ISO standardizes container sizes

test.source: ISO 668, first edition 1968

steps.note: Standards work began in the early 1960s, before the Vietnam contract.

steps.claim: Cheap freight helps manufacturing move to Asia

test.reason: trade economists find containerization raised trade sharply (e.g. Bernhofen, El-Sahli and Kneller, 2016); one of several drivers

steps.claim: Old manual ports decline: Manhattan's piers, London's Docklands

test.source: London's Docklands closed in stages, 1967–1981; the LDDC was set up in 1981

steps.note: Not instant: a decline over about 15 years.
steps.link_why: histories tie the closures to containerized ports downriver

steps.claim: Abandoned docks become Canary Wharf

test.source: Canary Wharf construction begins, May 1988

steps.note: Hudson Yards is built over rail yards, not abandoned piers, so it is not an example.
steps.link_why: Canary Wharf was built on the closed West India Docks

title: Ammonia synthesis and the nitrogen in us (1909)

steps.claim: Fritz Haber synthesizes ammonia from air

test.source: demonstration at Karlsruhe, July 1909

steps.claim: Carl Bosch scales it up at BASF's Oppau plant

test.source: Oppau plant starts production, Sept 1913

steps.link_why: BASF licensed and scaled Haber's process

steps.claim: Synthetic nitrates keep Germany's explosives flowing in WWI

test.source: German munitions supply after the British blockade, 1914–18

steps.note: 'Prolonged the war' is a historians' judgment, widely held.
steps.link_why: Haber-Bosch ammonia replaced blockaded Chilean nitrate

steps.claim: After the war, synthetic fertilizer spreads

test.source: Haber-Bosch plants built across Europe and the US in the 1920s

steps.link_why: the same process, turned to agriculture

steps.claim: Borlaug breeds semi-dwarf wheat that thrives on fertilizer

test.source: Borlaug's Mexico program crosses in Norin 10 dwarfing genes, 1953

steps.link_why: the varieties were bred to use heavy fertilizer without lodging

steps.claim: The Green Revolution reaches India and Pakistan

test.source: large seed imports to India and Pakistan, 1965–66; Borlaug's Nobel Peace Prize, 1970

steps.claim: World population grows from 1.6 billion to 8 billion

test.source: UN: world population reaches 8 billion, 15 Nov 2022

steps.note: Fertilizer is one of several drivers alongside medicine and sanitation.

steps.claim: About half the nitrogen in human bodies comes from Haber-Bosch

test.source: Vaclav Smil, Enriching the Earth (2001): an estimate

steps.note: An estimate from global nitrogen budgets, not an isotope measurement.

title: The Broad Street pump and modern sanitation (1854)

steps.claim: Cholera kills hundreds in Soho

test.source: outbreak from 31 Aug 1854; over 500 deaths in ten days

steps.claim: John Snow maps the deaths around the Broad Street pump

test.source: Snow's investigation, Sept 1854; dot map published 1855

steps.claim: The pump handle is removed

test.source: Board of Guardians removes the handle, 8 Sep 1854

steps.note: Officials did not accept Snow's water theory at the time; the outbreak was already waning.

steps.claim: The Great Stink fills Parliament with sewage smell

test.source: hot summer of 1858

steps.note: Parliament acted on the smell, under the miasma theory Snow opposed, not on his water evidence.

steps.claim: Bazalgette's intercepting sewers are approved

test.source: Metropolis Management Amendment Act, Aug 1858; construction from 1859

steps.link_why: the act responded to the Great Stink

steps.claim: London's sewers are completed and cholera fades

test.source: main system largely complete by 1875; the 1866 outbreak hit an unconnected area

steps.claim: Cities worldwide build sewers and filtered water

test.reason: New York, Paris and others built systems in the late 1800s and early 1900s; many sources of inspiration

steps.claim: Clean water helps drive a 30-year rise in life expectancy

test.source: Cutler and Miller, Demography 2005: clean water explains about half of the urban mortality decline in early-1900s America

steps.note: A major driver, alongside vaccines, antibiotics and nutrition; not the only one.
